title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes classify the boundary strata of the stable compactification \hat M_{g,ν} by 'MD-graphes', i.e. stable dual graphs. Vertices α carry a genus g_α and an order \tilde μ_α (number of branches, i.e. half-edges plus marked points). The stratum attached to a graph G is the 'multiplicité modulaire' \tilde M_G. It is the quotient, as a stack ('multiplicité'), of the product of the rigidified moduli spaces \hat M^!_{g_α,\hat ν_α} by the automorphism group Γ of the graph. Its modular dimension is Σ_α (3g_α − 3 + \hat ν_α). Trivalent genus-0 vertices (type (0,3)) contribute a point.

The previous page showed that modular dimension 2 forces one of two shapes. Either all vertices are of type (0,3) except one, of type (0,5) or (1,2). Or all are (0,3) except two, each of type (0,4) or (1,1).

This page lists the resulting five possibilities (74), with the action of Γ in each:
- \hat M^!_{0,5}: Γ acts through Γ → S_{\hat I_{α0}} ≅ S_5, permuting the 5 branches.
- \hat M^!_{1,2}: Γ acts through Γ → S_2.
- \hat M^!_{0,4} × \hat M^!_{0,4}: Γ acts through S_8. The NB refines this: Γ actually lands in Z/2 ⋉ (S_4 × S_4) = S_4 ≀ S_2, the stabiliser of the partition of 8 branches into 4+4. The Z/2 can exchange the two factors.
- \hat M^!_{0,4} × \hat M^!_{1,1}: Γ acts through S_4.
- \hat M^!_{1,1} × \hat M^!_{1,1}: Γ is said to act trivially.

Modular dimension 1 gives (75): \hat M^!_{0,4}, with Γ acting through S_4, and \hat M^!_{1,1}, with Γ acting trivially. Relative to these, the genuinely new cases in dimension 2 are \hat M^!_{0,5} and \hat M^!_{1,2}. So there are essentially four 'elementary' building blocks for modular dimension ≤ 2: M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,2}.

Grothendieck then states his expectation. A more or less complete understanding of the discrete fundamental groups (analytic context: orbifold π_1, i.e. mapping class groups and their boundary-stratum inertia) in these four cases should give the key to the general case. The next page starts carrying this out: specialisation diagrams of strata, beginning with \hat M^!_{0,4} ≅ P^1_Z and its three boundary points.
errors: The fifth case of (74) says Γ acts trivially on \hat M^!_{1,1} × \hat M^!_{1,1}. As stated in general this is a gap. When the two genus-1 vertices are graph-symmetric, Γ contains an involution exchanging the two factors. Example: g=2, ν=0, two elliptic tails joined at a node, giving the stratum (M̄_{1,1} × M̄_{1,1})/S_2 in M̄_2. Γ then acts through Γ → Z/2 by swapping factors, just as in the (0,4)×(0,4) case treated in the NB. The statement is only correct if the marking makes the two vertices distinguishable.
Minor: in the (0,4)×(0,4) case the line first says Γ → S_8. The NB correctly sharpens this to the half-direct (wreath) product Z/2·(S_4×S_4). Γ need not surject onto either group.

ideas.what: Classification of codimension-≤2 boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν} by stable graphs. Each stratum is a quotient of a product of moduli of types (0,5), (1,2), (0,4)×(0,4), (0,4)×(1,1), (1,1)×(1,1) by the graph automorphism group.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification by stable graphs; boundary strata as quotients ∏ \bar M_{g_v,n_v} / Aut(G)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); standard in later work (e.g. Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths)
ideas.where_published: Only implicitly in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2 on the Teichmüller tower and 'modular dimension'.

ideas.what: Notion of 'modular dimension' and the reduction to four elementary cases M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,2} (modular dimension ≤ 2).
ideas.modern_name: First two levels of the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Expectation that the discrete (analytic) fundamental groups of the four elementary cases, with their boundary structure, give the key to all g, ν.
ideas.modern_name: Two-level principle: mapping class groups have a presentation generated and related in levels ≤ 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck (Esquisse). Proved via Hatcher–Thurston and Harer; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000) 'On the Teichmüller tower of mapping class groups'. Profinite/GT side: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Nakamura–Schneps, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps.

ideas.what: The automorphism group of two (0,4)-vertices embeds in the wreath product S_4 ≀ S_2 ⊂ S_8.
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of a block decomposition; wreath product

missed.claim: This is a working draft of the 'two-level principle' later announced in Esquisse d'un programme. The page shows how Grothendieck arrived at the four elementary cases: via a dimension count on stable graphs, keeping track of Γ-actions on rigidified moduli. It also shows he initially framed the principle for discrete (analytic) π_1 rather than profinite π_1. This is of historical interest, but the content is in the published Esquisse and has since been proved (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; GT literature). Nothing mathematically new.
missed.quote: J'ai l'impression qu'une compréhension plus ou moins complète de la structure des Π, discrets (i.e. dans le contexte analytique) impliqués dans ces cas, donnera la clef pour une compréhension complète dans le cas général.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the genesis and original (discrete-first) framing of the two-level principle; useful for historians, not for current research.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine enumeration of codimension-2 strata of \bar M_{g,ν}, plus the earliest formulation of the two-level principle. That principle is published in Esquisse d'un programme and was later proved by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and others. The only notable details are the analytic/discrete emphasis and a small oversight about the factor swap in the (1,1)×(1,1) case.
transcription_corrections: Margin at top left reads 'Multiplicités modulaires de dim 2 (\tilde M_G)'. The first word is struck out and rewritten.
The small '29' above 'opère' appears to be a stray number or page marker, not part of the formula.

Line 4 of (74): there is a struck-out scribble before \mathfrak S. The surviving text seems to be 'Γ → \mathfrak S^{4}_{\hat I_{α0}} ≃ \mathfrak S_4', with a superscript 4 written over a deleted expression.
'Cela fait en tout essentiellement quatre cas' — the reading 'quatre' is consistent with the four elementary cases M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,2}.
The left marginal note by (75) is probably '(pas très intéressants!)' or '(peu intéressants!)'. It is only partially legible.
